conclusion_text:
## Cross-Cutting Findings from 11 Experiments

**1. Plausible order-flow narratives are not surviving out-of-sample, regardless of directional thesis.**
Underlying assumption failing: that a coherent story about *why* a price/volume pattern should predict continuation ("committed buyers absorbing supply," "trapped longs forced to liquidate," "laggards catching up to breadth thrust") is enough to generate a real edge once you can articulate it and confirm it in-sample/walk-forward.
Evidence: EXP-001/002 (gap-and-go, momentum-continuation thesis), EXP-003/004 (PDH fade, mean-reversion thesis), EXP-005/006 (breadth-thrust, relative-strength thesis) — three *opposite* theses (continuation, fade, relative-strength) all cleared in-sample/walk-forward checks and then produced negative OOS expectancy (-312, -162, -208, -50, -43 per trade). The direction of the bet doesn't matter; something about the validation methodology itself is passing hypotheses that don't hold up.
Implication: Stop treating "good in-sample/walk-forward" as a signal worth reporting at all — it has now failed to predict OOS sign 6/6 times. The next round should either (a) require a genuinely held-out, chronologically later test as the *first* gate before any parameter tuning, or (b) treat in-sample fit as evidence of overfitting risk rather than edge, especially given how easy it is to construct a narrative that fits recent history.

**2. Layering filters onto a weak base signal reduces trade count, not loss-per-trade — it doesn't fix anything.**
Underlying assumption failing: that trend filters, fundamentals screens, and volume-confirmation thresholds "clean up" a mediocre base strategy by removing bad trades and keeping good ones.
Evidence: ORB-3 (daily trend filter: win rate 47.6%→47.7%, trades halved, loss halved proportionally), ORB-4 (fundamentals filter made recent-60-day result *worse*, -0.64%→-2.42%, because it removed some of the better performers), ORB-5 (volume confirmation made win rate *and* R:R worse as the threshold tightened, 45.1%→38.9%). In every case the filter acted like random thinning of the sample, not selection for quality.
Implication: Don't keep bolting incremental filters onto a base mechanism that itself has no demonstrated edge (ORB never showed OOS positive expectancy in

## Additional Cross-Cutting Findings (beyond the established review)

**3. Mechanism designs with 3+ stacked conjunctive conditions are collapsing to statistically meaningless sample sizes before they ever get a fair OOS test.**
Underlying assumption failing: that adding more "confirming" conditions to a story (gap up AND above-average volume AND no VWAP retrace AND holds past 15 min; or PDH poke AND rel-vol spike AND two consecutive 5-min closes) makes the signal more precise without destroying its frequency.
Evidence: EXP-001 produced only 4 total trades (holdout below the 5-trade minimum); EXP-003 produced 0 trades in any window. In both cases the "reject" was really a "could not test" — the conjunction of rare conditions on a 29-symbol universe over the test window starved the sample before edge could even be evaluated. EXP-005/006 (breadth-thrust, also multi-condition) had enough trades to compute expectancy but still needed two rounds to get there.

## Additional Cross-Cutting Findings (beyond the established review, incorporating EXP-007/EXP-008)

**4. Both "continuation" and "reversion" stories built on the same underlying data (price/volume, same-instrument or index-breadth) fail OOS at similar rates — the direction of the bet is not the problem.**
Underlying assumption failing: that the lab just hasn't found the right *side* to play yet (momentum vs. fade). Look across the roster: EXP-001/002 (gap-and-go continuation, long bias) failed OOS; EXP-003/004 (failed-breakout fade, short bias) failed OOS; EXP-005/006 (relative-strength catch-up, bidirectional long/short) failed OOS; EXP-007/008 (VWAP-extension fade, bidirectional) failed OOS. That's every directional archetype available in a simple ORB-adjacent design space, all landing on negative OOS expectancy. This symmetry across opposite theses is itself informative: it's not that "breakouts fail so fades should work" or vice versa — both fail similarly, which points away from "wrong direction" as the diagnosis and toward "the signal-generation layer itself (intraday price/volume patterns on 5–15min bars for this universe) carries little real predictive content," at least in the way it's been operationalized so far.
Implication: Stop treating "try the opposite/mirror-image mechanism" as a fresh hypothesis. A mirrored fade of a rejected continuation idea (or vice versa) is not meaningfully novel and should not consume a full experiment slot unless there's a distinct causal story with a different data source, not just a sign-flip of the same VWAP/PDH/gap logic.

**5. "Wait for N confirming bars before entry" designs (a specific recurring sub-pattern of the already-flagged conjunction problem) fail for a distinct additional reason: lag, not just sample starvation.**
Underlying assumption failing: that requiring 2 consecutive 5-min closes/candles to "confirm" exhaustion or trend-holding improves signal quality for free. EXP-003 (two consecutive 5-min closes above PDH) → 0 trades; EXP-004, same mechanism → OOS expectancy -208.87; EXP-007 (two consecutive 5-min candles failing to print new extreme) → only 5 trades; EXP-008, same mechanism → 0/3 walk-forward windows positive. In every one of these four, the confirmation requirement was the specific ingredient (distinct from generic volume/fundamentals filters seen in the ORB seeds) that either starved the sample or arrived too late — by the time two bars confirm exhaustion/deceleration, the reversion/continuation move it's trying to catch has typically already happened, so the entries harvest the tail of the move rather than the move itself.
Implication: Treat "N-bar confirmation" as a red-flag mechanism component going forward, not a neutral quality filter. If a hypothesis needs multi-bar confirmation to define its entry, budget for the fact that this both shrinks the sample (per finding #3) *and* independently degrades expectancy through lag — two separate failure modes stacking, not one. Prefer single-bar, immediately-actionable triggers, or justify confirmation bars with an explicit lag-tolerance argument before running the full validation cycle.

**6. Threshold-sweeping on a single underlying signal family (ORB target multiple, volume multiple, ATR-extension multiple) has never once produced a config that is both statistically adequate and OOS-robust — it only ever trades overfitting-to-stale-data against sample collapse.**
Underlying assumption failing: that a fixed mechanism can be rescued by finding the "right" parameter value. SEED-ORB-2's sweep found a config that worked on 6 months but lost on the most recent 60 days. SEED-ORB-5's sweep found win rate and reward:risk *both* degrading as the threshold tightened, with trade counts falling to 18-29. EXP-007→EXP-008 tightened/held an ATR-extension multiple and went from 5 trades (can't validate) to 0/3 positive walk-forward windows (validated-and-failed). In three independent signal families now, sweeping a continuous threshold parameter has never surfaced a stable edge — it has only ever revealed the same over-fit/under-sampled dilemma in different clothing.
Implication: Deprioritize "sweep a threshold on an already-rejected or borderline mechanism" as a way to generate the next experiment. If round 1 of a mechanism is borderline, a parameter sweep alone should not count as sufficient additional evidence to greenlight it — the next hypothesis needs a structurally different signal (e.g., cross-sectional/relative-value ranking, order-flow/depth-based, options-derived positioning, overnight/gap information combined differently) rather than a retuned version of VWAP-distance, volume-multiple, or target-multiple on the same OHLCV bars. All 13 experiments so far have drawn their signal exclusively from same-instrument or index-breadth OHLCV data at 5–15 min resolution; that entire data-source class has yet to produce one durable OOS edge, which is reason enough to require the next batch to source signals from outside it.

EXP-009/EXP-010 (Intra-Sector Pair Spread Reversion, the first market-neutral pairs hypothesis, run through the new research_lab/pairs_simulator.py engine): REJECT on sample size (25 trades in 240 days, 1 OOS trade). Code-verified root cause: the hypothesis's own eligibility rule, trailing-60-day daily-return correlation > 0.8, is almost never satisfied by real NSE large-cap same-sector pairs -- HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK 0% of days, SUNPHARMA/CIPLA 0%, ULTRACEMCO/AMBUJACEM 9%, BAJFINANCE/SHRIRAMFIN 13%, TCS/INFY 49% (median correlations 0.4-0.6, only TCS/INFY ~0.8). Treat any future hypothesis whose gate assumes >0.8 daily-return correlation between two NSE stocks as sample-starved by construction. The z-score trigger itself was NOT the constraint.

EXP-011/EXP-012 (End-of-Day Reversal, Baltussen/Da/Soebhag 2025 -- the first hypothesis sourced from the academic literature rather than proposed by the Quant Researcher, and the first judged NET of transaction costs via research_lab/transaction_costs.py): REJECT. The effect itself replicates on NSE at roughly the published size -- 9,312 trades over 240 days, GROSS P&L +Rs.18,873 (~1 bp per position), in line with the paper's 2-3.5 bps per leg -- but Zerodha intraday charges plus a 2 bps/side spread cost Rs.257,403 (~14 bps per round trip), so the net result is -Rs.238,530 with 0/3 walk-forward windows positive. ESTABLISHED RULE (agreed 2026-09-07): an Indian cash intraday round trip costs ~10-14 bps regardless of position size (STT alone is 2.5 bps on the sell side), so any intraday hypothesis needs a documented GROSS edge of at least ~15 bps PER TRADE to be worth a full experiment. Every well-documented pure-intraday effect with data available to this lab (end-of-day reversal, market intraday momentum, interday half-hour momentum) sits in the 1-7 bps range and fails this bar by construction; the only candidates that clear it are event-driven (earnings-day moves) and those need announcement-TIME data the lab does not have. Intraday research is therefore paused in favour of swing research, where the same cost is negligible against multi-percent moves. Pool D continues as a framework test only.

EXP-082 (Crypto Cross-Sectional Momentum, Liu/Tsyvinski/Wu 2022 -- the first crypto-lane experiment, Pool F, 40 Binance USDT pairs 2021-09 to 2026-09, 1,000 USDT book, judged NET of 0.30%/side fees + 10 bps spread and India's 31.2% per-profitable-trade VDA tax with no loss set-off): REJECT, 0/2 walk-forward windows positive, out-of-sample expectancy -2.81 USDT/trade, evidence quality HIGH (90). The effect did not replicate even RAW in this sample: 1,812 trades, zero-cost engine P&L -556 USDT (CAGR -15%, win rate 45.5%) against BTC buy & hold +720 USDT (CAGR +11.5%). Costs then compound it: weekly rebalancing of ~8 slots turned the book over ~50x/year, so fees+spread cost 1,418 USDT over 5 years (~28%/yr of starting capital) and the no-offset tax took 2,911 USDT from 825 winners while 987 losers gave no relief -- pre-tax P&L -1,974, post-tax -4,885 USDT. ESTABLISHED RULES for every future crypto candidate: (1) the verdict is always post-tax, with pre-tax recorded alongside; (2) weekly-or-faster turnover is disqualified up front -- at 0.8% round-trip cost and 31.2% tax on each winner, a strategy needs holding periods of weeks to months (roughly <12 round trips per slot per year) and a raw win rate or payoff well above the equity norm, because the tax is asymmetric per trade; (3) the large-cap 40-coin cross-section is where LTW's momentum is weakest -- any cross-sectional crypto hypothesis needs either a wider universe (with real liquidity limits disclosed) or a time-series formulation on the majors.

EXP-083 / EXP-084 (Crypto Trend Timing -- Faber 2007's 10-month SMA rule on BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, 20% sleeves, month-end decisions only, Binance 2017-09 to 2026-09, 1,000 USDT book, judged NET of 0.30%/side fees + 10 bps spread and India's 31.2% per-profitable-trade VDA tax with no loss set-off): EXP-083 REJECT, EXP-084 PASS. The two runs have IDENTICAL rules, costs, tax, universe and Auditor; the only difference is an engine warm-up: EXP-083 computed the 10-month SMA inside each 3-year walk-forward window, so every window was blind for its first ten months (28% of the window) and the out-of-sample window missed the 2023-24 up-leg entirely (OOS expectancy -13.45 USDT/trade); EXP-084 computes the SMA on full history and passes it into each window as an extra column -- the same mechanism every cross-sectional strategy already uses for its ranks -- giving 3/3 windows positive post-tax, OOS +59.46 USDT/trade (16 trades), 44 trades total, evidence quality MODERATE (58.8). Full period (both runs, the continuous run is not windowed): 38 trades, average hold 178 days, win rate 37%; raw +17,044 USDT, fees 462, tax 6,689 (39% of raw gains because losers get no relief), PRE-TAX +16,582 (CAGR 37.5%, max DD 19%), POST-TAX +9,893 USDT (CAGR 30.4%, Sharpe 0.48, max DD 29%). Context that must travel with the PASS: (1) BTC buy & hold over the same period made +18,591 USDT pre-tax (CAGR 39%) with an 83% drawdown -- the rule buys drawdown control, not extra return, exactly as Faber documents; (2) the 20% protective stop is NOT in the source and fired on 23 of 38 exits; (3) the record is 44 trades -- MODERATE evidence, and a 9-year crypto sample is two cycles. Promoted to Pool F paper trading (SW-020) per the standing Pool F direction; the paper book reports pre-tax and post-tax P&L side by side.

EXP-085 (Crypto Time-Series Momentum, Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012's 12-month sign rule on BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, month-end decisions, 20% sleeves, no volatility scaling, Binance 2017-09 to 2026-09, judged NET of fees and India's 31.2% no-offset VDA tax, signal warmed up from full history like EXP-084): PASS, but a weaker one than the Faber rule it was built to cross-check -- 1/2 consistency windows positive (exactly the 50% floor; window 1, 2017-2020, lost -276 USDT post-tax), OOS +16.04 USDT/trade over 15 trades, 44 trades, evidence MODERATE (58.0). Full period: 40 trades, average hold 172 days, win rate 30%; raw +4,739, fees 193, tax 2,338, PRE-TAX +4,547 USDT (CAGR 21.0%, max DD 29%), POST-TAX +2,208 USDT (CAGR 13.8%, Sharpe 0.34, max DD 32%) -- against EXP-084's post-tax +9,893 (CAGR 30.4%) on the same coins, sleeves, stop, costs and tax. What this establishes: the Pool F trend PASS is a property of the trend signal, not an artefact of one rule's form, since both forms clear the post-tax audit; and the 10-month SMA form is materially stronger than the 12-month return-sign form on this sample, mainly because the sign rule stays long deep into a bear phase until the trailing-year return turns negative, while the moving-average rule exits earlier. Both rules will hold the same coins most months, so running a second Pool F book on this rule would double the same exposure with a weaker signal -- registered PASS, left in RESEARCH, not promoted; re-consider only as a replacement for, not an addition to, SW-020 if SW-020's paper record disappoints.

EXP-086 (Downside Beta, Ang/Chen/Xing 2006 -- 252-day daily-return beta on market-down days vs Nifty 50, TOP quintile long-only, 21-trading-day single-vintage hold, 8% stop, 10 positions; Nifty 500, 3 years fetched 2023-09 to 2026-09 with the first year used only as estimator warm-up, walk-forward judged 2024-09-13 to 2026-09-11): PASS, evidence quality HIGH (83.3): 253 windowed trades, 1/2 consistency windows positive (the 2024-09 to 2025-05 window lost -6,444 on Rs.10L), out-of-sample +152.69/trade over 87 trades. Full judged period: 248 trades, win rate 39.5%, average hold 22 days, CAGR 4.71%, Sharpe 0.37, max DD 24.7% -- BELOW the Nifty 500 index (CAGR 11.7%) and buy-and-hold over the same two years; the edge sits entirely in the 2025-26 windows. Two things the record must carry: (1) the roadmap profile had the direction backwards (long LOW downside beta) and was corrected to the paper's premium side before the run; (2) the warm-up mechanism (judge the walk-forward from one year after the data start) was introduced here and should be the standard for any strategy with a lookback near a window's length. Verdict PASS is honest under the frozen Auditor, but the economics are weak: a risk premium that pays only in up-legs, at a 40% win rate. Registered PASS, left in RESEARCH pending the promotion decision.

Naming note (2026-09-14, per direction): the crypto paper pool built as 'Pool F' on 2026-09-13 (EXP-082..085, SW-019..SW-021) is now 'Pool E' -- state under deployment/state/pool_e/, run_pool_e.py, reporting/pool_e.py. Every earlier record that says Pool F refers to this pool.

EXP-087 (Crypto Volatility-Managed Exposure, Moreira/Muir 2017 -- always long BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, each 20% sleeve scaled by min(1, (60%/sigma)^2) on the previous 30 days' realized volatility, monthly exit-and-re-enter rebalance with a 10% band, 20% stop, Binance 2017-09 to 2026-09, judged NET of fees and India's 31.2% no-offset VDA tax): REJECT, evidence HIGH (90): 340 windowed trades, 1/2 consistency windows positive post-tax (both positive PRE-tax), OOS -3.19 USDT/trade over 105 trades. The cleanest demonstration yet of what the tax does: full period 335 trades, average hold 36 days, raw +13,163 USDT (CAGR 34%, Sharpe 0.81, max DD 46% vs BTC buy & hold's 83%) and PRE-TAX +10,683 USDT (CAGR 31%, Sharpe 0.74) -- the volatility-timing mechanism WORKS on coins -- but the monthly rebalance books a taxable gain in every profitable month, so tax took 12,694 USDT (96% of raw gains: 154 winners taxed, 181 losers no relief) and POST-TAX is -2,011 USDT. ESTABLISHED RULE (sharpens the post-EXP-082 rule): under India's per-trade VDA tax the binding constraint is not turnover in trades per year but the NUMBER OF TIMES A GAIN IS REALISED. A rule that resizes or re-forms a winning position every month pays tax on each leg with no relief on the losing legs, and a 46% win rate with modest per-trade gains cannot survive that. Only rules that HOLD a winner across many months (trend rules with 170+ day average holds -- EXP-084/085) keep enough of the gain. Any future crypto candidate must therefore realise gains no more than a few times a year per coin; monthly-rebalanced weighting schemes are disqualified up front, however good their pre-tax Sharpe. Registered REJECT (SW-023).

EXP-088 (Realized Low Volatility -- NSE's Nifty100 Low Volatility 30 methodology: 1-year daily log-return volatility, bottom decile of the Nifty 500 long-only, 126-trading-day single-vintage hold, 8% stop, 10 positions; 5 years fetched 2021-09 to 2026-09, first year warm-up, walk-forward judged 2022-09-14 to 2026-09-11): REJECT, evidence HIGH (79.1). Both consistency windows positive (2022-09 to 2024-01: 28 trades, +47,584, win rate 75%; 2024-01 to 2025-05: 49 trades, +19,284) but the out-of-sample window (2025-05 to 2026-09) lost -7,550 over 36 trades at a 28% win rate, expectancy -209.72/trade. Full judged period: 101 trades, CAGR 10.3%, Sharpe 1.07, max DD 17% -- the best risk-adjusted equity result since SW-013 on the full period, still below the Nifty 500's 11.7% CAGR, and it stopped working in the most recent 16 months. Same shape as Betting Against Beta (SW-009): the risk-based family produced returns on NSE through the 2022-24 period and decayed after -- now seen twice with different constructions (beta, total volatility) and once inconclusively (idiosyncratic volatility, SW-012). ESTABLISHED: no further risk-based (low-beta / low-volatility) candidates on this universe until a new regime has a record; the family's remaining roadmap entries (Nifty Alpha Low Vol 30 blend) inherit this. Registered REJECT (SW-024).

Pool F opened 2026-09-16 per direction: Pool A's twin with PARTIAL PROFIT BOOKING -- every active Pool A strategy also runs on its own fresh Rs.1,00,000 book under deployment/state/pool_f/ with the same class, universe, data, next-day-open fills and sizing; the ONE difference is deployment.paper_trading_engine.PartialBookingConfig (trigger 5%, book half at the trigger level, stop on the remainder raised to entry from the next day; stop takes priority on a day that touches both). Pool A and the strategy rules are untouched (standing rule). The 5% / half numbers were chosen a priori, not optimised, and are disclosed as such. Purpose: a live, book-by-book comparison of 'as published' vs 'with partial booking' over the coming months, to answer the observed pattern of positions going green and finishing red.

EXP-089 (Crypto Weekly Trend Timing -- SW-020's own Faber 10-month SMA rule, checked/rebalanced weekly (every Sunday UTC) instead of monthly, same five majors, 20% sleeves, 20% stop, Binance 2017-09 to 2026-09, judged NET of fees and India's 31.2% no-offset VDA tax; built 2026-09-17 after direction for more visible crypto activity than a once-a-month book): PASS, evidence MODERATE (73.2). 72 windowed trades, 1/2 consistency windows positive, OOS +45.75 USDT/trade over 29 trades. Full period: 67 trades (vs SW-020's 38 on the identical coins/period), raw +20,248, fees 931, tax 8,673 (only 19 of 67 trades profitable, taxed; 48 losers no relief), PRE-TAX +19,318 (CAGR 39.8%, Sharpe 0.55, max DD 29%), POST-TAX +10,645 USDT (CAGR 31.4%, Sharpe 0.52, max DD 42%). Reading against SW-020 (post-tax +9,893, CAGR 30.4%, max DD 29%): weekly checking found marginally MORE post-tax profit and CAGR on this sample, at the cost of a materially worse drawdown (42% vs 29%) and a lower win rate (28% vs 37%) -- more frequent decisions caught trend changes faster in the coins' favour often enough to cover the extra tax, but with rougher realised volatility. Both are real, PASS-verdict, HIGH-to-MODERATE-evidence trend rules on the same coins; they will usually agree on direction, so running both live mostly doubles the same exposure rather than diversifying it -- same caveat already recorded for SW-021. Registered PASS (SW-028); promoted to a third Pool E book per direction (visible weekly activity was the explicit ask), with that overlap disclosed.

EXP-090 (Moving Average Pullback, SW-014's own ported prototype rules -- 20/50-day MA uptrend, 1.5%-band pullback, green reaction candle, pattern stop, 20-day-high fixed target at >= 1.8x reward:risk; first walk-forward test since being ported to Pool A on 2026-09-06 on an informal 5yr/26-symbol backtest alone): REJECT, evidence HIGH (87.2). 0/2 consistency windows positive. Full judged period (2 years): 221 trades, CAGR 3.77%, Sharpe 0.31, max DD 24% -- below buy-and-hold (4.56%) and well below the Nifty 500 index (11.6%). The informal prototype backtest (242 trades, 37.6% win rate, net +Rs.5,830 over 5 years) did not survive a real walk-forward test on the frozen NSE 500 universe.

EXP-091 (Crypto Daily Trend Timing -- SW-020's Faber rule checked/rebalanced EVERY day instead of monthly or weekly, completing the monthly/SW-020, weekly/SW-028, daily cadence set): PASS, evidence HIGH (83.9). 151 windowed trades, 3/3 consistency windows positive, OOS +20.97 USDT/trade over 60 trades -- the strongest audit signal of the three cadences. Full period: 146 trades, POST-TAX +14,001 USDT (CAGR 35.1%, Sharpe 0.44, max DD 42%) vs SW-020 monthly's +9,893 (CAGR 30.4%, DD 29%) and SW-028 weekly's +10,645 (CAGR 31.4%, DD 42%) on the identical coins/period. Win rate only 18% (26 of 146) -- daily checking realises many more small losing exits than the slower cadences (fees+tax: 2,593 + 12,554 of the 29,148 raw gain), and the post-tax edge survives only because the 26 winners run far. Pattern across all three cadences: faster checking monotonically increases both post-tax return AND drawdown/realised-loss frequency on this sample -- the CAGR gain from daily over monthly (35.1% vs 30.4%) is real on this record but comes with a much rougher, much-lower-win-rate ride and 4x the trade count. Registered PASS (SW-029); promoted to a fourth Pool E book per the same direction as SW-028, with the overlap and the low-win-rate caveat disclosed.

EXP-092 (Volume-Backed Breakout, SW-015's own ported prototype rules -- close above the prior 20-day high on >=1.5x normal volume, pattern stop, fixed 2x reward:risk target; first walk-forward test since being ported to Pool A on 2026-09-06 on an informal 5yr/26-symbol backtest alone): REJECT, evidence HIGH (90.0). Out-of-sample expectancy -113.09/trade over 99 trades -- negative on genuinely unseen data, the most important single check, and it fails it. Full judged period: 289 trades, CAGR -22.19%, Sharpe -1.29, win rate 27.7%, max DD 45.79% -- a heavy loser, well below buy-and-hold (4.56%) and the Nifty 500 index (11.62%). Walk-forward windows themselves split (window 1: -38.44% CAGR; window 2: +3.82% CAGR), but the OOS check settles it. The informal prototype backtest (415 trades, 37.1% win rate, net +Rs.11,507 over 5 years) did not survive a real walk-forward test on the frozen NSE 500 universe -- the same failure mode as MA Pullback (EXP-090), ported the same day.
